Zombie Girl: Keep the Lights On

First of all, it’s really hard to judge the game and developer, since I have no idea how difficult it is to make a game on UE5. I can’t tell what’s a base preset and what’s handcrafted – models, mechanics, or AI behavior. The fact is, the game is solid and playable, yet has plenty of room for improvement.

Right now, it has two game modes: Story and Defense. The first is a corridor shooter, while the second is a wave-based survival mode. I started with Story, got lost in the second stage, and was about to write a negative review, criticizing the slow cover-based gameplay against soldiers and overly easy fights against blind and deaf zombies.

But then I tried Arena mode, where the game truly shines. It’s quick, fast-paced, and has roguelike elements that force you to adapt to survive against different enemies. The game keeps surprising you: first arena – humans, second arena – zombies, what’s next? Humans and zombies combined? Nope! Friggin’ werewolves and giant spiders!

I highly recommend playing Defense mode first, as it not only helps you get used to the controls, understand the mechanics, and test different guns – it also unlocks weapons for story mode and character skins.

Now that I’ve beaten Defense and almost finished Story, I can confirm that the game is worth both its price and your time. Yes, it’s “just” a shooter on UE5 – anyone could make one, you might say. 
Anyone could, but this developer actually did it. 
And I really want to see how the game grows and improves.
(One thing bothers me, though: the game hasn’t received any updates in 2025 atm, I hope it hasn’t been abandoned.)

By the way, I’ve seen many negative reviews complaining about the misleading “sexual content” tag. It’s true – there are  no H-scenes or fully nude characters. The most you’ll get is protagonist’s damaged uniform. But compared to other crappy NSFW games, this dev got the priorities right: gameplay first, lewdness second.
